title: Successive hitting-time identity
statement: Let $G$ be a finite $D$-regular multigraph with $D>0$, and let $s,t$ be distinct vertices. For each $N\ge0$, let $H_N(t,v)$ be the sum, over $0\le j<N$, of the probabilities that a uniformly chosen indexed-neighbor walk of length $j$ from $v$ avoids $t$ at every visited vertex, including its endpoint. Let $A H_N(t,s)$ be the average of $H_N(t,\cdot)$ over the $D$ indexed neighbors of $s$. Then $H_{N+1}(t,s)=1+A H_N(t,s)$.
hypotheses_covered: $G$ is a finite regular multigraph of degree $D$
